segments.text: Your breath stinks. Which one is worse? Gum or mouthwash? Most sugar-free gums are made with a gum base, but here's the catch. US labeling allows manufacturers to list this as a single proprietary ingredient. What's usually in there is a petroleum-based polymer, the same family of plastics that are used in inner tubes. Sugar-free gum can reduce your risk for cavities, but it doesn't kill bacteria. In fact, it can actually trap it. One study showed over 100 million bacteria in a single chewed piece.

Antiseptic mouthwash works by killing bacteria directly. A meta-analysis showed it reduced plaque by 32%, gingivitis by 24%. This is on top of brushing compared to a placebo rinse. But, it's not all good. It also kills the bacteria that converts nitrate to nitric oxide, which is used to regulate your blood pressure. If I was forced to choose between gum and mouthwash, I would brush my teeth.
